    Journal Articles

    Assistive technologies for supporting wellbeing of older adults

    Published in PETRA: Pervasive Technologies Related to Assistive Environments, 2021

    Over the coming decades, the societal goal of maximizing the number of older adults who experience positive aging trajectories has been established. To achieve this, innovative technology-based interventions tailored to older adults’ functional levels and focused on healthy lifestyles are considered essential. This work presents a cluster of digital solutions aimed at supporting and maintaining healthy, independent living for older adults who face permanent or temporary reductions in functionality and capabilities.

    Recommended citation: Dratsiou et al. (2021). "Assistive technologies for supporting wellbeing of older adults." Proceedings of the 14th PErvasive Technologies Related to Assistive Environments Conference.(pp. 338-341).

    Conference Papers

    EMOROBCARE: A Low-Cost Social Robot for Supporting Children with Autism in Therapeutic Settings

    Published in ICSR, 2025

    The EMOROBCARE project aims at developing a low-cost, expressive social robot designed to support therapy for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder. This paper presents the system software design and development tools. We illustrate an example use case game that combines perception, speech, reasoning, and expressive capabilities of the robot. Additional games will be developed through co-design with therapists in order to foster communication and emotional expression.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, S., Pou, B., Mayoral-Macau, A., Redondo, A., Rios, D., & Ros, R. (2025) "EMOROBCARE: A Low-Cost Social Robot for Supporting Children with Autism in Therapeutic Settings." International Conference on Social Robotics. (pp. 607-615). Singapore: Springer Nature Singapore.

    TIAGo Head: an AI Powered Platform for Social Robotics

    Published in RO-MAN, 2025

    This paper presents the TIAGo Head, a new tabletop social robot from PAL Robotics, focusing on its capabilities as an HRI platform. We detail the robots’ hardware, highlighting its sensors/actuators and on-board computing; and its software architecture, including social perception, expressive face, a knowledge base, and integration with large language models (LLMs) for natural conversations. We also describe a use-case in a receptionist scenario where TIAGo Head dynamically interacts with travelers by displaying news and conversing.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, S., Lemaignan, S., Ros, R., Ferrini, L., Gebellí, F., Juričić, L., ... & Ferro, F. (2025) "TIAGo Head: an AI Powered Platform for Social Robotics." 2025 34th IEEE International Conference on Robot and Human Interactive Communication (RO-MAN). (pp. 1099-1106). IEEE.

    Design of embodied mediator haru for remote cross cultural communication

    Published in ICRA, 2024

    While social robots for children have mostly focused on traditional education such as language, science, and math, applications promoting cultural competency are rare. This paper presents a robot-mediation framework for cross-cultural communication, enabling a social robot to act as a mediator between schoolchildren from different countries. A participatory design activity by an interdisciplinary team defined the robot’s roles, design, and technical requirements, which were then used to build the prototype system. A pilot study with high school students in Japan and Australia demonstrated the system’s potential to engage children in communicating, sharing, and discussing cultural themes with their remote peers.

    Recommended citation: Gomez, Randy, et al. (2024). "Design of embodied mediator haru for remote cross cultural communication." 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) .(pp. 5505-5511).

    Design of social features for robot-mediated cross-cultural interaction

    Published in HRI, 2024

    In this paper, we design a hierarchical set of socio-emotional features to understand the effect of cross-cultural mediation facilitated by a social robot between two remote groups of schoolchildren in Japan and Australia. We also equip the robot with behaviors that maximize children’s participation and stimulate socio-emotional interaction, which in turn increases the chance of observing the designed features. Differences were observed between the cultures (AUS and JP), suggesting the need for future adaptation of the framework to different cultures as the pilot is expanded to more countries.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, S., Gomez, R., Szapiro, D., & Merino, L. (2024) "Design of social features for robot-mediated cross-cultural interaction." Companion of the 2024 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction. (pp. 351-355).

    Challenges of deploying assistive robots in real-life scenarios: an industrial perspective

    Published in RO-MAN, 2023

    With increasing life expectancy and staff shortages, understanding the needs of older adults and exploring emerging fields such as social robotics has become urgent. This paper highlights the importance of cognitive and physical support, reducing loneliness, increasing social engagement, and alleviating caregiver burden, and discusses how socially assistive robots (SAR) can help address these needs. It also identifies key challenges in the design and deployment of SAR systems, emphasizing the importance of end-user involvement to improve acceptability and adoption. Finally, the paper describes PAL Robotics’ approaches to real-world deployment of the ARI and TIAGo social robots and presents examples of their use in addressing diverse healthcare needs.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, S., Ros, R., & Lemaignan, S. (2023). "Challenges of deploying assistive robots in real-life scenarios: an industrial perspective." 2023 32nd IEEE International Conference on Robot and Human Interactive Communication (RO-MAN) . (pp. 435-442).

    Open-source natural language processing on the pal robotics ari social robot

    Published in HRI, 2023

    We demonstrate how state-of-the-art open-source tools for automatic speech recognition (Vosk) and dialogue management (Rasa) can be integrated on a social robotic platform (PAL Robotics’ ARI) to enable rich verbal interactions. Our open-source, ROS-based pipeline follows the ROS4HRI standard, and the demonstration details the integration to allow replication on other robots. The work is presented in the context of assistive robotics and elderly care—domains with unique interaction challenges for which ARI has been designed and extensively tested in real-world settings.

    Recommended citation: Lemaignan, Séverin, et al. (2023). "Open-source natural language processing on the pal robotics ari social robot." Companion of the 2023 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction.(pp. 907-908).

    Towards the deployment of a social robot at an elderly day care facility

    Published in ICSR, 2022

    Life expectancy is increasing with time, and with it, more support is needed to provide care for the elderly. Social robots may in this context support therapy, monitoring, or entertainment activities. This paper describes current work on deploying our social robot ARI at an elderly day care centre, focused on promoting engagement in the routines carried out at the centre. By using a user-centred design approach, the paper presents the prototype development process of three activities and their initial validation in a 2-day pilot study. The preliminary results highlight an increasing responsive behaviour of the elderly towards the robot on day 2 compared to day 1 in one of the activities. In contrast, in a second activity, the robot was mostly ignored, suggesting that further work must be done in terms of attracting the attention of the user, and not giving for granted that the mere presence of a robot will suffice to trigger curiosity towards initiating interactions.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, S., & Ros, R. (2022) "Towards the deployment of a social robot at an elderly day care facility." International Conference on Social Robotics. (pp. 277-287).

    Towards using Behaviour Trees for long-term social robot behaviour

    Published in HRI, 2022

    This paper introduces a Behaviour Tree based design of long-term social robot behaviour in the context of SHAPES project, using ROS-compatible libraries, specifically two types of behaviours: a robot idle behaviour where the human approaches and begins the interaction, and a second behaviour where the robot actively navigates and searchers for a specific user to deliver a reminder. The behaviours will be tested on-site as part of SHAPES pilots and adjusted based on feedback and needs and is focused on long-term robot acceptance.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, Sara, and Séverin Lemaignan. (2022) "Towards using behaviour trees for long-term social robot behaviour." 2022 17th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI). (pp. 737-741).

    Social robotic application to support active and healthy ageing

    Published in RO-MAN, 2021

    With the global population aging and the number of healthcare users requiring support increasing, optimizing and supporting independent living for older adults is crucial. This paper reviews the needs and challenges of older adults who prefer to age healthily at home and explores how socially assistive robots (SAR) can help. The focus is on the social robotics application developed for the H2020 SHAPES project, using PAL Robotics’ ARI, a high-performance social robot designed for multi-modal expressive gestures, gaze, and personalized behavior. ARI is integrated with digital solutions from the SHAPES project to enhance human-robot interaction and user acceptability for independent living support. Validation will take place at Clinica Humana (Mallorca, Spain), and this paper describes the scenario, validation plan, and strategies to improve user engagement during pilot assessments.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, Sara et al. (2021). "Social robotic application to support active and healthy ageing." 2021 30th IEEE International Conference on Robot & Human Interactive Communication (RO-MAN). (pp. 1074-1080).

    An EEG investigation on planning human-robot handover tasks

    Published in ICHMS, 2020

    Human–robot joint action is essential in applications where robots collaborate with humans on physical tasks. While robots are designed to model and predict human actions, little is known about how humans represent a robot’s actions within their own action plans. This paper presents a combined psychological and HRI user study in the context of human–robot handover tasks. Results show a positive user experience, with participants adopting gaze patterns similar to those observed in human–human handovers. EEG analysis indicates increased motor readiness during robot handovers compared to solo actions, suggesting heightened planning demands in human–robot interaction. These findings highlight the role of gaze as an effective non-verbal communication cue in HRI and provide new insights into the neural mechanisms underlying human–robot joint action.

    Recommended citation: Cooper, S., Gow, S., Fensome, S. F., Dragone, M., & Kourtis, D. (2020). "An EEG investigation on planning human-robot handover tasks." 2020 IEEE International Conference on Human-Machine Systems (ICHMS) . (pp. 1-6).

    ARI: the Social Assistive Robot and Companion

    Published in RO-MAN, 2020

    With the global population aging and the rise of patients with multiple chronic conditions, healthcare costs are increasing, making the optimization of hospital and in-home care crucial. This paper reviews the challenges faced by older adults, people with mobility constraints, hospital patients, and isolated healthcare users, and explores how socially assistive robots can support them. The focus is on PAL Robotics’ ARI, a high-performance social robot designed for multi-modal expressive gestures, gaze, and personalized behavior. ARI has potential in healthcare for providing first-care assistance and emotional support, especially to isolated users such as the elderly or patients confined due to infectious diseases like COVID-19. Its technical features and potential applications are discussed.

    Recommended citation: Cooper et al. (2020). "ARI: the Social Assistive Robot and Companion." 2020 29th IEEE International conference on robot and human interactive communication (RO-MAN). (pp. 745-751).
